items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: I remember Leo Parker was playing alto saxophone on that... [in Coleman Hawkins' band] ... Leo Parker was here then, because he had left the Eckstine band, and Leo came up with his baritone and sat in with... I furnished the rhythm section for them.

ctx.x: think Coleman Hawkins went into the Three Deuces, and Hot Lips Page came into the Yacht Club. The bands were always switching around like that.

I remember one time Coleman Hawkins had a band in a place called Kelly's Stables. Once they recorded this thing with Dizzy Gillespie, and I remember Leo Parker was playing alto saxophone on that. "Disorder At The Border" -- there were four sides they did, I think.

There was just music everywhere. Moreso, there were musicians that you could actually, between sets, go around to a bar they had called the White Roses where everybody congregated, and guys would go around there and just drink. And you know, standing next to Art Tatum or whomever, or shaking hands with this one and saying "Hello" to this one... For a young musician, you really felt like you were into something.
